mainTopic: Who pays for the חביתין of a כהן גדול who died before a replacement is appointed, the verse sources for each view, and whether רבי שמעון's rule is Torah law or a court rule.
overview: A new משנה asks who pays for the כהן גדול's daily חביתין after he dies, before a new כהן גדול is appointed. רבי שמעון says the community pays, and רבי יהודה says his heirs pay. Either way, the offering is brought as a full עשרון. The גמרא brings a ברייתא with each תנא's verse source. רבי יהודה uses 'מבניו' and 'אותה'. רבי שמעון uses 'חק עולם' and 'כליל תקטר'. The גמרא then checks that every word in the verses has a job in each view, which brings in a גזירה שוה on 'כליל'. Next it asks how רבי שמעון can call public funding a Torah law, when a משנה in שקלים quotes him calling it a rule of בית דין. רבי אבהו explains that there were two rules. The Torah law said public funds. The court briefly moved the cost to the heirs, and then returned to the Torah law. The גמרא then challenges the next rule on that list, that there is no מעילה for the ashes of the פרה אדומה, since this seems to be a Torah law already. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the previous derivation
steps.stepSummary: The text quotes the last words of the earlier discussion: the חביתין is learned from a 'meal offering that comes as one עשרון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: …a meal offering that comes as one tenth, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the discussion from before. That discussion learned the rules of the כהן גדול's חביתין from another meal offering that is also one עשרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that the חביתין is one עשרון of flour. So it is compared to a meal offering of the same size, not to one of two or three עשרונים. The word וכו׳ tells us the full phrase was already stated earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering (made of flour)
One tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the phrase is already known

phrases.english: A meal offering that comes as one tenth, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the derivation carried over from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חביתין is compared to another meal offering of the same size, one עשרון.

steps.title: The משנה: who pays when no new High Priest was appointed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks who pays for the חביתין if no new כהן גדול was appointed. רבי שמעון says the community, רבי יהודה says the heirs, and the offering is brought as a full עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: If they did not appoint another priest in his place, whose property was it offered from? רבי שמעון says: from the community's. רבי יהודה says: from the heirs'. And it was offered whole.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה asks whose money pays for the dead כהן גדול's daily offering until a new one is appointed. Two תנאים give two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול pays for his own חביתין. Once he dies, the question is whether the obligation moves to the public (רבי שמעון) or stays with his family (רבי יהודה). The משנה also says that during this time the offering is a full עשרון, not split in halves.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
In his place, as his replacement
The community, paid from public funds
Heirs, here the dead כהן גדול's family
Whole, meaning a full עשרון

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section explains where each view comes from: רבי יהודה's, that the heirs pay, and רבי שמעון's, that the community pays. It also explains why the offering is brought whole.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If they did not appoint another priest in his place,
phrases.notes: This continues the earlier case of a כהן גדול who died.

phrases.english: from whose property was it offered?
Rabbi Shimon says: from the property of the community.
Rabbi Yehuda says: from the property of the heirs.
And it was offered whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מִינּוּ כֹּהֵן אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו, מִשֶּׁל מִי הָיְתָה קְרֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the case of the כהן גדול who died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רבי שמעון says the community pays and רבי יהודה says the heirs pay. In this period the offering is brought as a full עשרון.

steps.title: ברייתא: the verse shows that the heirs pay
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how we know the heirs pay for the חביתין, and answers from the verse 'the anointed priest in his place from among his sons shall offer it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught: If a כהן גדול died and they did not appoint another priest in his place, how do we know his meal offering is brought from the heirs' property? The verse says: 'And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons shall offer it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the verse source for רבי יהודה's view that the heirs pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the חביתין mentions 'his sons.' The ברייתא reads this as a sign that the family carries on the obligation. So in the gap before a new כהן גדול, the heirs bring it, not the public.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From where do we know? (asking for a source)
'The verse teaches', which introduces the source
The anointed priest, the כהן גדול
From among his sons

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
A High Priest who died
and they did not appoint another priest in his place,
from where do we know that his meal offering is offered
from the property of the heirs?
The verse teaches:
"And the anointed priest in his place
from among his sons shall offer it."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא מִנְחָתוֹ קְרֵיבָה מִשֶּׁל יוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse source for רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the חביתין is brought from the heirs' property when no new כהן גדול has been appointed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:15: 'And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons shall offer it.'

steps.title: The heirs bring the whole amount, not half
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the heirs might bring the offering in halves. It rejects this from the word 'it': the whole offering, not half. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they should offer it in halves. The verse says 'it', meaning all of it and not half of it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe the heirs split the offering in halves the way the כהן גדול does. It answers from the word 'it' that they must bring the full עשרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול offers his עשרון in two halves. The word 'it' (אֹתָהּ) is read as 'all of it.' So the heirs bring the complete amount, which matches the משנה's words 'it was offered whole.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might have thought', which introduces a possible mistake
Halves
'It', the word in the verse being explained
All of it and not half of it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, after the כהן גדול dies and before a new one is appointed, his heirs pay for the חביתין. They bring a full עשרון, not halves. Both points come from the verse in ויקרא 6:15.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Whole' here does not mean the heirs bring an extra or different offering. It means they bring the full עשרון instead of splitting it into halves the way the כהן גדול normally did.

phrases.english: One might think they should offer it in halves?
The verse teaches "it":
all of it and not half of it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives the source for the משנה's ruling that the offering is brought whole.
steps.raayaObject: That the heirs bring the full עשרון rather than halves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'אֹתָהּ' in ויקרא 6:15, read as 'all of it.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heirs might bring the offering in halves, the same way the כהן גדול did.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heirs must bring the full עשרון.

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the verse: the community pays, and the whole offering is burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from 'חק עולם' that the community pays for the חביתין, and from 'כליל תקטר' that all of it is burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'A statute forever (עולם)' means it comes from the property of the 'world', the community. 'It shall be wholly burned' means all of it is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי שמעון's source for his view in the משנה that the community pays for the חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the word עולם as 'the world', meaning the public. Since the community is now paying and not a כהן, you might think the offering could be eaten. So he uses 'כליל תקטר' to show that the whole thing is still burned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A statute forever'; רבי שמעון reads עולם as 'the world', meaning the community
From what belongs to the public, paid by the community
'It shall be wholly burned'; the entire offering goes on the מזבח
Burning an offering on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the heirs pay (from 'הכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו'). רבי שמעון says the community pays (from 'חק עולם').

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"A statute forever [olam]": from that of the world,
phrases.notes: He's playing on the word עולם, which can mean 'forever' or 'the world', meaning the whole community.

phrases.english: "It shall be wholly burned":
that all of it should be burned on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״חׇק עוֹלָם״ – מִשֶּׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא's source, after רבי יהודה's source in steps 3-4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה that the community pays and the full offering is burned

steps.title: Challenge: Is the 'anointed priest' verse really coming to teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה can use 'הכהן המשיח' to teach that the heirs pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does this verse, 'the anointed priest', really come to teach this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's source. This line sets up the next step, which will show the verse is needed for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse that is already needed for one teaching is not free to teach a different law. The גמרא is about to argue that 'והכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו' is used for another purpose, so רבי יהודה's proof may fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed כהן, meaning the כהן גדול
'Is it for this that it comes?' This asks whether a verse is really meant to teach this law.

phrases.english: And this verse, "the anointed priest"
phrases.notes: This is the verse רבי יהודה used in step 3 to teach that the heirs pay.

phrases.english: is it for this that it comes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's source from step 3 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's use of 'והכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו' to teach that the heirs pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is needed for a different teaching, so it cannot also be the source for the heirs paying.

steps.title: A ברייתא: אהרן and his sons each bring their own offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the plural 'they shall offer' that אהרן and his sons bring separate offerings, and that 'בניו' refers to ordinary כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for what a ברייתא teaches. 'This is the offering of אהרן and his sons which they shall offer to ה׳ on the day he is anointed.' You might think אהרן and his sons bring one offering together. So the verse says 'which they shall offer', plural: אהרן brings his own, and his sons bring their own. 'His sons' means ordinary כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge, showing what the 'anointed priest' verse is really used for. This first part explains the earlier verse (6:13).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Verse 13 says 'offering' in the singular, which could suggest one shared offering. The plural 'they shall offer' shows that each brings his own. The ברייתא also says 'בניו' means ordinary כהנים, which sets up the next step, where verse 15 is needed to prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, meaning the verse is already used for another teaching
'One might think': introduces a possible wrong reading
'The verse says': introduces the wording that rules out the wrong reading
By himself, separately
Ordinary כהנים, not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: That verse is needed for that which is taught in a baraita:
"This is the offering of Aaron and his sons

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ לַה׳ בְּיוֹם הִמָּשַׁח אֹתוֹ״,
phrases.english: which they shall offer to the Lord on the day he is anointed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13

phrases.english: One might think that Aaron and his sons
bring one offering together?
The verse states: "Which they shall offer to the Lord,"
phrases.notes: The point is the plural 'they shall offer', even though 'offering' was singular.

phrases.english: Aaron brings one by himself,
and his sons bring theirs by themselves.
"His sons": these are the ordinary priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing the ברייתא that backs up the challenge in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that the 'anointed priest' verse is already used for another teaching

steps.title: The 'anointed priest' verse is needed to show that 'his sons' means ordinary priests
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that 'בניו' in verse 13 means ordinary כהנים, because verse 15 already speaks about the כהן גדול. So verse 15 is used up and seems unavailable to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means ordinary כהנים, but maybe it means only כהנים גדולים? When the verse says 'And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons', the כהן גדול is already mentioned. So how do I explain 'his sons'? It means ordinary כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its proof, and in doing so it uses up the verse 'והכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו'. This is the heart of the גמרא's challenge to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since verse 15 already covers the כהן גדול's offering, 'בניו' in verse 13 must mean ordinary כהנים. Verse 15 is therefore needed to teach the כהן גדול's basic obligation to bring the offering. That leaves the question: where does רבי יהודה get his rule that the heirs pay?

keyTerms.meaning: 'You say X, or perhaps it is only Y?': tests a reading against another option
'When it says': brings another verse to settle the question
This is already stated, so there is no need to teach it again
'How do I explain?': what does this word come to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two verses. Verse 13 ('this is the offering of Aaron and his sons') is now about ordinary כהנים. Verse 15 ('the anointed priest in his place') is about the כהן גדול's regular obligation, which is exactly why רבי יהודה's use of it is being questioned.
steps.whyThisMatters: If verse 15 is fully used for the כהן גדול's basic obligation, then רבי יהודה needs another way to explain how he learns that the heirs pay.

phrases.english: Do you say it means ordinary priests,
or is it only High Priests?
When it says
"And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15. This is the same verse רבי יהודה used.

phrases.english: the High Priest is already mentioned,
so how do I explain "his sons"?
These are the ordinary priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֹּהֲנִים הֶדְיוֹטוֹת, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 7 and shows exactly how verse 15 is used up.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge from step 6 that 'הכהן המשיח' is not free for רבי יהודה's teaching
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא using ויקרא 6:15 to show that 'בניו' in 6:13 means ordinary כהנים

steps.title: The extra letter in 'מבניו' shows the פסוק teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said 'בניו' (his sons). It says 'מבניו' (from among his sons), so it teaches two lessons: the כהן גדול's obligation and that the heirs pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it only meant one thing, the פסוק should have written 'the anointed כהן in his place, his sons shall do it.' Why 'from among his sons'? Learn from it two lessons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 8. The פסוק is not used up, because its extra wording lets it teach two lessons at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8, the פסוק seemed fully taken by the lesson about the כהן גדול himself. Here the גמרא points to the extra letter מ in 'מבניו'. A shorter wording would have been enough, so the extra letter adds a second lesson for רבי יהודה: the heirs bring the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From among his sons'. The extra letter מ is the source of the second lesson.
The anointed כהן, meaning the כהן גדול
Learn from it two things: one פסוק teaches two lessons

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
"The anointed priest in his place, his sons shall do it."
phrases.notes: This is the shorter wording the פסוק could have used. The real פסוק, ויקרא 6:15, says 'מבניו'.

phrases.english: What is "from among his sons"?
Learn from it two things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Steps 6 and 8, that the פסוק seemed unavailable to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: one פסוק yields two lessons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is fully used up teaching the כהן גדול's own obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra מ in 'מבניו' adds the lesson that the heirs bring the offering.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with the word 'אותה'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learned from 'אותה' that the whole offering is brought, not half. רבי שמעון learns that from 'כליל תקטר', so what does he do with 'אותה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what does he do with this word 'it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון and asks what he learns from the word 'אותה'. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the תורה should teach something. Since רבי שמעון gets his lesson from a different phrase (Step 5), the word 'אותה' seems to have no job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It'. רבי יהודה used this word to teach 'the whole offering' (Step 4).
'What does he do with it?' What lesson does this תנא learn from that word?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, this word "it":
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַאי ״אֹתָהּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבי יהודה's source, the גמרא now checks רבי שמעון's use of רבי יהודה's word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי שמעון learns from 'אותה'.

steps.title: 'אותה' teaches the case of a כהן גדול who died mid-day
steps.stepSummary: If a כהן גדול died after offering the first half and a new one was appointed, the new one must bring a full עשרון. He may not bring only half from home, and he may not use the first כהן גדול's leftover half.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for a כהן גדול who died, and they appointed another in his place: he should not bring half an עשרון from his house, and not the half עשרון of the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון uses 'אותה' for a special case: the כהן גדול died partway through the day's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין is a full עשרון of flour, split in half: half offered in the morning and half in the afternoon. If the כהן גדול dies in between, the new כהן גדול cannot finish with just a half portion. 'אותה', 'it', means a complete offering, so he must start a full new עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the amount of flour for the חביתין
Half of that amount, which is offered in the morning or in the afternoon
From his house, meaning from his own funds
He needs it for, meaning the word is used to teach a different lesson

phrases.english: He needs it for a High Priest who died
and they appointed another in his place,
phrases.notes: The case is that he died after offering the morning half, before the afternoon half.

phrases.english: that he should not bring half a tenth from his own house
nor the half-tenth of the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותה' teaches that a replacement כהן גדול must bring a whole new עשרון, not half from home or the leftover half of his predecessor.

steps.title: Why not learn this from 'ומחציתה'?
steps.stepSummary: The same lesson about a replacement כהן גדול was already learned from the extra ו in 'ומחציתה'. So why does רבי שמעון need 'אותה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from 'and half of it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 11. That lesson already has a different source, so 'אותה' would be unnecessary for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (on 50b), the extra ו ('and') in 'ומחציתה' was read as teaching that the new כהן גדול brings a full עשרון. If so, 'אותה' is again left with no job for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it from...', meaning there is already a source for this
'And half of it' (ויקרא 6:13). Its extra ו was expounded earlier.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from "and half of it"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13. Back on 50b, the extra ו at the start of this word taught the same rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון needs 'אותה' for the replacement כהן גדול case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lesson that already has a source does not need a second one, so 'אותה' would still be unused.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not expound an extra ו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not learn anything from the extra letter ו, so he needs 'אותה' for this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not expound a ו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does not draw lessons from an added ו. So 'ומחציתה' teaches him nothing extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether an extra ו carries meaning is a matter of how a תנא reads פסוקים. For רבי שמעון the ו is just normal wording. That leaves 'אותה' as his source for the replacement כהן גדול rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not expound the letter ו, meaning he gives it no extra meaning

phrases.english: He does not expound the vav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different rule of reading: this תנא does not expound an extra letter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra ו in 'ומחציתה' already teaches the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון does not expound a ו, so he learns the rule from 'אותה'.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns 'the whole offering, not half' from 'כליל תקטר', and uses 'אותה' for the כהן גדול who died mid-day, because he does not expound an extra ו.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'חק עולם'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learned from 'חק עולם' that the community pays. רבי יהודה says the heirs pay, so what does he learn from these words?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, what does he do with this phrase 'a permanent law'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question in the other direction: what does רבי יהודה learn from רבי שמעון's source? This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, רבי שמעון used 'חק עולם' to teach that the community pays for the חביתין. רבי יהודה disagrees, so the phrase seems to have no lesson in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A permanent law'. רבי שמעון's source that the community pays (Step 5).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, this phrase "a statute forever":
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״חׇק עוֹלָם״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 10, now asking about רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יהודה learns from 'חק עולם'.

steps.title: 'חק עולם' simply means the law is permanent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads 'חק עולם' plainly: the law of the חביתין applies forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: It shall be a permanent law forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה takes 'חק עולם' at its simple meaning: this offering is a permanent law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not read 'חק עולם' as teaching who pays. For him it only says the חביתין obligation never stops. That fits his view that the heirs pay, not the community.

keyTerms.meaning: It will be a law forever, meaning a permanent obligation

steps.whatToRemember: Each תנא has a job for every word. For רבי יהודה, 'אותה' means a whole offering, 'מבניו' means the heirs pay, and 'חק עולם' means a permanent law. For רבי שמעון, 'חק עולם' means the community pays, 'כליל תקטר' means a whole offering, and 'אותה' covers the replacement כהן גדול.

phrases.english: It shall be a statute forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יהודה, 'חק עולם' teaches that the חביתין obligation is permanent, not who pays.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה learn from 'it shall be wholly burned'?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון used 'כליל תקטר' for his own rule, the גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with these words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'it shall be wholly burned'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same pattern as the last question. It asks what רבי יהודה learns from the words 'כליל תקטר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון used these words to teach that the whole offering is burned. רבי יהודה already learns that the whole offering is brought from the word 'אותה' (step 4). So the words seem extra for him, and the גמרא wants to know their purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It shall be wholly burned', meaning the whole offering goes on the מזבח
'Why do I need it?' Asks what a phrase in the Torah comes to teach

phrases.english: Why do I need 'it shall be wholly burned'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15. The question is asked according to רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 14, now about a second phrase in the passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה derives from 'כליל תקטר'

steps.title: He needs it for a ברייתא about two offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה needs 'כליל תקטר' for a ברייתא. The ברייתא starts with what each passage teaches on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא. I only know that the upper offering (the כהן גדול's מנחה) must be wholly burned. I also know that the lower offering (an ordinary כהן's מנחה) may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה needs the words for a ברייתא. The ברייתא begins by stating what each of the two passages teaches by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper passage (ויקרא 6:15) is about the כהן גדול's חביתין and says 'it shall be wholly burned'. The passage right below it (ויקרא 6:16) is about an ordinary כהן's מנחה and says 'it shall not be eaten'. Each passage gives only one rule, and the ברייתא is setting up a way to share them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it' for a different teaching
The upper passage, about the כהן גדול's חביתין
The lower passage, about an ordinary כהן's מנחה
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
'It shall not be eaten'

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
I only have the upper one
phrases.notes: 'Upper' means the passage that comes first in the פסוקים, ויקרא 6:15.

phrases.english: (the כהן גדול's offering) with 'it shall be wholly burned',
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. Either way, 'upper' means the כהן גדול's offering.

phrases.english: and the lower one (an ordinary כהן's offering)
with 'it shall not be eaten'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by pointing to a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words are needed for a ברייתא that links the two offerings.

steps.title: How do we apply each passage's rule to the other?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know to apply each offering's rule to the other offering as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know to apply what is said about this one to that one, and what is said about that one to this one?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is asked. How do we know that both rules apply to both offerings? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is a two-way swap. The ordinary כהן's מנחה should also be wholly burned. The כהן גדול's חביתין should also be forbidden to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?' Asks for a source

keyTerms.term: לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
keyTerms.meaning: To apply what is said about one case to the other case

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what is said about this one to that one
and what is said about that one to this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the separate rules to asking how to combine them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that each offering's rule also applies to the other

steps.title: The word 'wholly' links the two offerings
steps.stepSummary: The word 'כליל' appears in both passages, which creates a גזירה שוה. Through it, both offerings are wholly burned and both are forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says 'wholly' and 'wholly' to make a גזירה שוה. 'Wholly' is said here, and 'wholly' is said there. Just as here it must be wholly burned, so too there it must be wholly burned. And just as there the פסוק adds a לא תעשה against eating it, so too here there is a לא תעשה against eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה built on the shared word 'כליל'. Each offering takes on the other's rule. This is why רבי יהודה needs 'כליל תקטר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Here' is the כהן גדול's חביתין, and 'there' is the ordinary כהן's מנחה. The ordinary כהן's מנחה picks up the rule 'wholly burned'. The כהן גדול's חביתין picks up a לא תעשה against eating it, so someone who eats it breaks a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching that links two passages because the same word appears in both
'Wholly, entirely', the shared word
A negative commandment (a prohibition)
'The פסוק teaches', introduces the source

steps.whatToRemember: Through the גזירה שוה of 'כליל', both the כהן גדול's חביתין and an ordinary כהן's מנחה are wholly burned, and there is a לא תעשה against eating either one.

phrases.english: The verse says 'wholly', 'wholly', for a גזירה שוה,
phrases.notes: The word 'כליל' appears in both ויקרא 6:15 and 6:16.

phrases.english: 'Wholly' is said here
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the כהן גדול's חביתין.

phrases.english: and 'wholly' is said there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ordinary כהן's מנחה.

phrases.english: just as here it falls under 'it shall be wholly burned',
so too there it falls under 'it shall be wholly burned'.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לְהַלָּן לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ,
phrases.english: And just as there the verse comes to place a prohibition on eating it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתָהּ.
phrases.english: so too here it comes to place a prohibition on eating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question in step 18. This also finishes the answer to step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'כליל' makes both rules apply to both offerings.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון hold community funding is Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. Does he really hold that paying for the חביתין from community funds is a Torah law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי שמעון hold that bringing it from community funds is Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון and asks a pointed question. This step sets up a challenge that the גמרא will develop next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון learned from 'חק עולם' that the community pays when there is no כהן גדול. Learning a rule from a פסוק makes it sound like Torah law. The question shows the גמרא doubts he really holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: From the community's funds
By Torah law
'And does he hold?' Questions a sage's position

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just asking for information. It is a challenge, and the גמרא will next bring a reason to think רבי שמעון does not hold this.

phrases.english: And does רבי שמעון hold
that bringing it from the community's funds is Torah law?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 5, where רבי שמעון learned from 'חק עולם' that the community pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִשֶּׁל צִיבּוּר דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יהודה and returns to רבי שמעון's position from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that the community pays for the חביתין, learned from 'חק עולם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Learning the rule from a פסוק makes it Torah law. The גמרא doubts רבי שמעון really holds that and is about to challenge it.

steps.title: The source for the challenge: seven rules of בית דין, starting with a gentile's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי שמעון lists seven rules set up by בית דין. The first case is a gentile who sends a עולה without paying for the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון said, בית דין set up seven rules, and this is one of them. If a gentile sent his burnt offering from overseas and sent נסכים with it, they are offered from his money. If not, they are offered from public funds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its challenge from step 20. It starts quoting a משנה where רבי שמעון lists rules that בית דין made, and this step gives the first example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'הִתְקִינוּ בֵּית דִּין', meaning these are rules the court set up. Anything on this list is a court rule and not a Torah law. The גמרא is building toward one item on the list that will cause the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: they set up or enacted (a rule)
the court (here, the rabbinic court that made rules)
wine and flour offerings that go along with an animal offering
from public funds (the Temple treasury)
a country overseas, far away

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: Rabbi Shimon said:
The court instituted seven things,
and this is one of them.
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to a rule in the משנה there (שקלים 7:6), about נסכים paid from public funds.

phrases.english: A gentile who sent his burnt offering from overseas,
if he sent libations with it,
they are offered from his own money,
phrases.notes: Some versions say קריבה (singular), in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is קריבין, 'they are offered', meaning the נסכים.

phrases.english: and if not, they are offered from public funds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה that backs up the challenge raised in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון treats certain public-funded offerings as court rules.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה שקלים 7:6, רבי שמעון's list of seven court rules.

steps.title: Another rule on the list: a convert who died and left offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if a convert dies and leaves offerings without נסכים, the נסכים are paid from public funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, a convert who died and left offerings: if he has נסכים, they are offered from his property. If not, they are offered from public funds.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going through רבי שמעון's list of court rules. This is a second example of public money covering נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the gentile, this convert's offerings would be missing their נסכים, so בית דין arranged for the public to pay. This step is still building up the list. The item that matters for the challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: a convert to Judaism
animal offerings
and he left behind

phrases.english: And similarly, a convert who died,
and left offerings:
if he has libations, they are offered from his own,
and if not, they are offered from public funds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same list of court rules.
steps.raayaObject: Further items on רבי שמעון's list of court rules.

steps.title: The key item: the כהן גדול's מנחה is paid from public funds by court rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says it is a condition of בית דין that if a כהן גדול dies and no replacement is appointed, his מנחה is paid from public funds. So רבי שמעון seems to hold this is a rabbinic rule, not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is a condition of the court: when a כהן גדול died and they did not yet appoint another priest in his place, his מנחה is offered from public funds.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line that creates the problem. רבי שמעון lists the public paying for the dead כהן גדול's מנחה as a rule of בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי שמעון learned from a פסוק that the חביתין come from public funds as a Torah law. Here he calls the same thing a 'condition of the court'. That looks like a contradiction, and רבי אבהו answers it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a condition set by the court
the High Priest
his meal offering (here, the חביתין)
they appointed

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the law itself. רבי שמעון says in both places that the public pays. The question is only whether, in his view, this comes from the Torah or from a court rule.

phrases.english: And it is a condition of the court,
a High Priest who died
and they did not appoint another priest in his place,
that his meal offering be offered from public funds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaches the item in the quoted משנה that directly contradicts רבי שמעון's Torah-law position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that the חביתין of a dead כהן גדול come from public funds by Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה רבי שמעון himself calls this a 'condition of the court', which means a rabbinic rule. That contradicts his reading of a פסוק as a Torah source.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: there were two separate rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that בית דין made two rules on this matter, one after the other. The next step explains what they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: There were two rules.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו defends רבי שמעון. He says there were two court rules, so the משנה calling this a court rule does not cancel the Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that if the משנה calls it a court rule, it cannot be Torah law. רבי אבהו says the court made two rules in a row about who pays. The next step explains them: the second rule brought things back to the Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: rules or enactments
there were

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
There were two ordinances.
phrases.notes: Some versions have שני, in round brackets; the corrected wording is שתי, in square brackets, which matches the feminine word תקנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in שקלים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: two separate rules rather than one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one rule, so it could not be both a Torah law and a court rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah law stands. The court made two rules: one moving the cost to the heirs, and a second one returning it to public funds.

steps.title: The history of the rule: public funds, then heirs, then back to public funds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains how the court rule came about. By Torah law the מנחה came from public funds. When the treasury ran low, the court made the heirs pay. When the heirs neglected it, the court went back to the Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, it came from the public funds. Once they saw that the chamber's funds were running low, they enacted that it be collected from the heirs. Once they saw that the heirs were negligent about it, they set it back on the Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אבהו's answer. It tells the history behind the court rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction in רבי שמעון. The Torah law, learned from the פסוק, said public funds pay. The court briefly changed this to the heirs, then cancelled its own change and went back to the Torah law. So the 'court rule' in the משנה is really the court restoring the Torah law after its temporary change.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
The public; here, public Temple funds
The Temple treasury chamber that held public funds
They enacted a rabbinic rule
Heirs (here, of the כהן גדול who died)
They were negligent

steps.whatToRemember: The rule went through three stages: Torah law (public funds), a court change (the heirs pay), and back to the Torah law. The משנה's 'court rule' is the court returning to the Torah law.

phrases.english: By Torah law, it was from the public funds.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן גדול's daily מנחה, which the Torah says comes from public funds when there is no כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Once they saw that the chamber's funds were running low,
they enacted that it be collected from the heirs.
Once they saw that the heirs were negligent about it,
they set it back on the Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִדְּצִיבּוּר, כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזוֹ דְּקָא מִידַּחְקָא לִישְׁכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבהו's answer by explaining how the two rules developed over time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical sequence: Torah law, then a temporary court change, then a return to the Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה calling it a court rule means רבי שמעון holds it is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a Torah law. The court rule is the court restoring the Torah law after cancelling its temporary change to the heirs.

steps.title: The next court rule: no מעילה for the ashes of the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה. בית דין ruled that a person is not liable for מעילה for using the ashes of the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And concerning the red heifer, that one is not liable for misusing its ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule in רבי שמעון's list in the משנה. This line sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה presents this as a rule made by בית דין. Normally, using הקדש for personal benefit is מעילה and requires a קרבן. Here the court says there is no מעילה for the ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used for purification
Liable for מעילה, the misuse of consecrated property
Ashes

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל פָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מוֹעֲלִין בְּאֶפְרָהּ
phrases.english: And concerning the red heifer, that one is not liable for misusing its ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל פָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מוֹעֲלִין בְּאֶפְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the same משנה of seven court rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By court rule, there is no מעילה for using the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

steps.title: But this is already a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that no מעילה for the ashes is already a Torah law. Why would the משנה call it a court rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is a Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It says this rule is already in the Torah, so it should not be listed as something בית דין made up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנאי בית דין is supposed to be something the court added. If the Torah itself already says there is no מעילה for the ashes, there was nothing for the court to add.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule set up by the court
It is a Torah law

phrases.english: But it is a Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the clause just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of 'no מעילה for the ashes' as a court rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah law cannot also be a court rule. If the Torah already exempts the ashes, the court did not need to make this rule.

steps.title: The ברייתא on 'חטאת היא'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point from a ברייתא. The פסוק calls the פרה אדומה a חטאת, so there is מעילה with it. The word 'היא' limits the מעילה to the animal itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'It is a sin offering' teaches that one is liable for misusing it. 'It': for it, one is liable for misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its challenge that the ashes are exempt by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'חטאת היא' teach that the פרה is treated like a חטאת, so using it is מעילה. The extra word 'היא' ('it') narrows this to the animal itself. That sets up the exclusion of the ashes, which comes next in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering; the פסוק gives the פרה אדומה this name
It teaches; this introduces what a פסוק comes to teach
A word in the פסוק that narrows a rule; here, 'היא'

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says there IS מעילה with the פרה. The point is that this applies only to 'it,' the animal itself, and not to its ashes.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "It is a sin offering,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:9

phrases.english: teaches that one is liable for misusing it.
"It": for it one is liable for misuse,
phrases.notes: The word 'it' narrows the rule: only the animal itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge that the ashes are exempt by Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: That 'no מעילה for the ashes' is a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'חטאת היא' (במדבר 19:9): the word 'היא' limits מעילה to the animal itself.
